body:
Structured outcome:
{
  "ceo_summary": "We are delivering a lean, high-performance Win32 native application that demonstrates core system integration without the overhead of modern frameworks.",
  "constraints": [
    "Must use C++20 standard.",
    "Must implement WinMain entry point.",
    "Must use RegisterClassEx, CreateWindowEx, and standard message loop.",
    "Must link against user32 and gdi32.",
    "Directory structure: include/CounterApp.hpp, src/CounterApp.cpp, src/main.cpp, root CMakeLists.txt.",
    "CMakeLists.txt must set C++20 and target_include_directories for include/.",
    "Headers must use PascalCase.",
    "No tests included.",
    "Self-contained implementation.",
    "Left-click in client area must increment an integer counter displayed in the window."
  ],
  "cpo_summary": "The code will be strictly organized with PascalCase headers and a clean separation of concerns between the window logic and the entry point.",
  "modality": "desktop_app",
  "rationale": "The brief explicitly requests a Win32 C++20 application with a graphical window, message loop, and direct OS API usage (user32, gdi32), which defines the desktop_app modality."
}

author: Stack (Arthur & Geoff (CEO & CTO))
body:

{
  "build_notes": "CMake 3.15+; C++20 standard; target_include_directories for include/; link user32 and gdi32; no tests; Windows Release build via build.bat",
  "cto_summary": "Geoff confirms the VRAM governor is stable for this lightweight Win32 workload, allowing full C++20 optimization without memory pressure.",
  "primary_language": "cpp",
  "risks": [
    "LSP verification timeouts on shadow includes (Vrammonitor.hpp) may delay CI feedback",
    "Win32 message loop must correctly handle WM_PAINT to reflect counter state without flicker",
    "PascalCase header naming must be strictly enforced to avoid shadow guard failures"
  ],
  "secondary_languages": []
}
